title: One idea, several companies
blurb: A description produced one company, because the disambiguation gate answers 'which company did you mean' and three companies every search returned score identically — a tie, and for a market a tie is the answer. What tells a market from a shared name is arithmetic on the reader's own words: one content word is a brand, two or more is a kind of thing. Every company in the report now carries the countable reason it is there, and every one left out carries which of four things happened to it — including the two that look identical from outside and are not.
